::: {.hero}

# Natural ecosystem loss behind consumption

BF-NEE links the loss of natural ecosystems through **agricultural expansion** to
the **commodities** grown on the new land and to **final demand** – here, consumption
in Germany. Results are available for every producing country, time period,
commodity and ecosystem type.

[Explore global trends](global.qmd){.btn .btn-light}
[Open the map](maps.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-light}

:::

## What is new in this version

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**`r sub(":.*", "", build_info$pipeline_version)`** (data built `r build_info$built_at`)

- **Intensive pasture (v3).** Cropland *and* intensive pasture count as agricultural
  land. Loss linked to pasture expansion is attributed to grazing livestock.

- **Commodity shares from expansion.** A crop's share is now its *increase* in area
  relative to the total increase of all expanding crops in the same period. Crops
  whose area shrank get a share of zero.
- **Agricultural-expansion constraint.** Only natural ecosystem loss that coincides
  with agricultural expansion in the same grid cell is attributed (Eq. 31–32).
- **Ecosystem classes are kept.** The constrained loss is split back onto the
  ecosystem classes in proportion to their original loss, so footprints by
  ecosystem type add up exactly to the total footprint.
:::
